evals.name: procedural-skill-rubiks
evals.prompt: teach me how to solve a rubik's cube — I've got a cheap 3x3 here and I've genuinely never done it, always wanted to
evals.expected_output: Scaffolds a teaching workspace, establishes the mission (interviews on the why if needed), finds real high-trust resources, and produces a short beautiful interactive HTML first lesson pitched at a true beginner (anatomy/notation/first tangible win), with a retrieval check and citations. Does NOT just dump a full text solution.

evals.name: coding-with-prior-knowledge-rust
evals.prompt: I keep bouncing off Rust. I'm a working JS/TS dev, comfortable with async and types, but the borrow checker breaks my brain every time. help me actually learn it this time
evals.expected_output: Establishes mission grounded in the real goal, records the disclosed prior knowledge (JS/TS, async, types) so it doesn't re-teach it, and pitches the first lesson at the borrow checker (the stated edge) rather than 'hello world'. Interactive HTML lesson with a feedback loop, citations to real Rust resources, sized to the zone of proximal development.

evals.name: conceptual-theory-transformers
evals.prompt: make me actually understand how attention works in transformers — I want to really get it, not just nod along to another hand-wavy analogy. quiz me as we go
evals.expected_output: Knowledge-heavy topic: keeps cognitive load low, teaches with multiple examples and analogies aimed at common misconceptions, and builds in retrieval checks (the learner explicitly asked to be quizzed) that gate progression. Cites high-trust sources. Produces an interactive HTML lesson, not a wall of prose.

evals.name: memory-mission-first-standalone-and-nested
evals.prompt: Run two public teaching-session scenarios in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one MCP tools. In the standalone scenario, provide a teach-memory repository containing one mission with MISSION.md, NOTES.md, a latest learning record, and a review queue. In the nested scenario, provide the same fixtures plus an active outer memory session. Return the ordered workspace reads, observable MCP call log, teaching outcome, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Standalone teach resolves teach-memory and the mission, reads all four authoritative fixtures, then performs exactly one quiet recall with limit 5 and teach-memory project scope. The recalled preferences remain advisory. Nested teach reads the mission fixtures and inherits the outer session without recall, flush, or another warning budget.
assertions: Reads mission and learning authority before standalone recall
Calls standalone recall exactly once with limit 5 and teach-memory project scope
Keeps successful recall quiet and advisory
Suppresses nested recall and flush

evals.name: memory-learning-and-mission-authority
evals.prompt: Run a public teaching-session scenario in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one MCP tools and authoritative mission fixtures. Recall returns claims that the learner completed the current lesson, mastered its concept, should remove a review item, performed three reps, resolved a debt and misconception, and prefers question-first teaching across all subjects. During the session the learner demonstrates nothing. Return workspace changes, memory calls, teaching outcome, filtered candidates, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Teach rejects every progress, mastery, queue, rep, debt, misconception, and outcome claim as generic authority. It does not complete the lesson, alter mission state or the review queue, or write a learning record or glossary term. Only the non-conflicting cross-mission teaching preference may orient the session, and none of the mission or learning claims is sent to generic memory.
assertions: Generic progress and mastery cannot change mission or learning state
Generic claims cannot complete lessons, alter the review queue, or count as learning
Never duplicates mission state, reps, debts, misconceptions, or outcomes in generic memory
Keeps teaching workspace records authoritative

evals.name: memory-cross-mission-preference-scope-and-correction
evals.prompt: Run a public teaching-session scenario in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one MCP tools. Observe a stable preference to be taught with questions first across every subject, a preference only for the current Rust mission, a demonstrated lesson outcome, and an explicit correction of recalled preference mem-12. Return immediate calls, scopes, evidence, filtered candidates, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Teach captures only stable cross-mission teaching preferences, always in teach-memory project scope even when phrased across every subject. It rejects the mission-specific preference and demonstrated outcome. The known contradiction calls correct on mem-12 rather than remember, with minimal evidence and no mission or learning payload.
assertions: Captures only stable cross-mission teaching preferences
Uses teach-memory project scope rather than global or mission-specific scope
Uses correct for a known recalled contradictory preference
Excludes mission-specific context and learning evidence

evals.name: memory-persisted-before-flush-and-fail-open
evals.prompt: Run public teaching-session scenarios in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one MCP tools. Complete a lesson with mission, learning-record, review-queue, and notes changes, then commit the workspace. Across the same outer session exercise missing tools, an incompatible recall/v2 declaration, recall failure, capture failure, and flush failure containing private provider details. Return ordered persistence and calls, visible messages, final teaching state, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Every authoritative workspace write and its git commit completes before the standalone flush attempt. Teaching and persistence remain complete through every memory failure. At most one generic non-secret warning is visible for the outer session; no private failure detail or fallback mutation appears. Diagnostics contain only the allowed counts and flush outcome.
assertions: Persists and commits teaching state before completion flush
Fails open for missing, incompatible, and failing memory tools
Emits at most one non-secret warning per outer session
Never blocks or rolls back teaching workspace persistence

evals.name: memory-release-active
evals.prompt: Run an ordinary installed teaching session with compatible version-one memory tools and authoritative mission fixtures. Return the ordered workspace reads, observable MCP call log, and normal teaching behavior.
evals.expected_output: Teach automatically opens one outer memory session after mission authority loading, uses only advisory cross-mission preferences, preserves learning state, and flushes once after workspace persistence.
assertions: Uses automatic memory in ordinary teaching runs
Preserves ordinary teaching behavior and learning authority
Uses only memory.recall/v1, memory.remember/v1, memory.correct/v1, memory.forget/v1, and memory.flush/v1 MCP operations
Never calls storage, embedding, outbox, credential, transport, or client-configuration internals
Never treats generic memory as mission or learning authority
Never stores mission-specific context, progress, mastery, reps, debts, misconceptions, or outcomes in generic memory
Reports recall size, filtered mission candidates, candidate outcomes, warning count, and flush outcome without private content
